title: EV Charging Cost in India: Price per kWh and Your Bill Explained
summary: Understand EV charging cost in India, including price per kWh for AC and DC charging, home charging costs, monthly expenses and state-wise EV tariffs.
body_markdown:
The number you see at a public EV charging station can look simple: **₹X per kWh** .


Then the charging session ends, and the final amount on the bill is different from what you expected.


If you’ve ever wondered why, the answer usually comes down to three things: **where you charge, what type of charger you use, and how much energy your vehicle actually needs** .


There isn’t one fixed **EV charging cost in India** . Home charging, public AC charging and public DC fast charging all work out differently. Your state tariff and, in some cases, the time at which you charge also matter.


So if you’re trying to work out what charging will actually cost you each month, don’t look at the charger rate alone.


Start with the number that appears everywhere in EV charging: **kWh** .


## **What Does kWh Mean on an EV Charging Bill?**


A kilowatt-hour, or **kWh** , is the standard unit used to measure electricity.


One kWh is one unit of electricity on your electricity bill. Your local DISCOM (Distribution Company) sets the applicable tariff and bills you for the electricity you consume.


For example, if your EV uses 10 kWh during a charging session and the applicable rate is ₹10 per kWh, the electricity portion works out to ₹100.


It gets a little less straightforward with public charging because the amount you pay can also include the operator’s service charge and GST.


That’s why two charging sessions using the same amount of electricity don’t always cost exactly the same.


## **What Is the Cost of EV Charging at Public Stations in India?**


Public EV charging stations typically charge:


**Charging type** **Typical rate**


Public AC slow charging ₹8–₹15/kWh


Public DC fast charging ₹15–₹25/kWh


These rates include the electricity tariff, operator service charge and GST.


The location also matters.


A charger at a highway rest stop can cost more than one in a city. Faster, higher-kW DC chargers also tend to carry a higher rate because you’re paying for a quicker charging experience.


So if you see two different prices on two charging stations, don’t assume one is wrong.


Look at the charger type and location first.


## **AC vs DC Charging: Why Does the Price Change?**


AC charging is slower and is commonly used at home or at public slow-charging points.


DC charging is faster and is generally used at public fast-charging stations. The typical rate of public AC charging is ₹8–₹15 per kWh and public DC fast charging is ₹15–₹25 per kWh.


Think about a normal commute.


If your vehicle is going to stay parked for a few hours, a slower charger can do the job. If you’re on a longer trip and want to get back on the road quickly, a **DC fast charger** is more useful.


You’re paying more per unit for public fast charging, but you’re also spending less time waiting.


If you regularly need faster charging, understanding the charger’s power output can help you choose the right option for your use case. Statiq offers[DC charging solutions](https://www.statiq.in/dc-chargers) designed for faster EV charging.


## **Home Charging Cost: What Changes Your Bill?**


Home charging gives you more control over what you spend.


Domestic electricity tariffs in most states range from around **₹3 to ₹10 per unit** , depending on the DISCOM and your consumption slab.


There is one thing worth watching closely.


Your EV doesn’t have a separate relationship with your household electricity bill unless you have a dedicated EV meter. Its consumption gets added to the rest of your household usage.


If you’re already using a high number of units every month, the additional EV consumption can push your household into a higher tariff slab.


So your actual **cost of EV charging at home** depends on more than the vehicle’s battery.


Your home’s total electricity consumption matters too.


For convenient home charging, **[Statiq Nectar](https://www.statiq.in/nectar)** is available in different power configurations to suit different home charging requirements.


## **What About Home EV Charger Installation Cost?**


For many electric two-wheelers, charging at home doesn’t require a dedicated charger installation.


A standard 5A household socket can be sufficient, particularly for scooters with removable batteries.


A wall-mounted Level 2 charger is a different setup.


The **home charging installation cost** depends on things such as your existing wiring, the charger brand and whether the electrical circuit needs an upgrade. Some DISCOMs also provide separate EV meter connections and dedicated tariffs.


If additional electrical load is required, the DISCOM needs to approve the increase.


## **How Do You Calculate Your Monthly EV Charging Cost?**


You can get a reasonable estimate without complicated calculations.


You need:


1. Monthly distance


1. Real-world range


1. Battery capacity


1. Electricity rate


Suppose you travel **900 km a month** and your scooter has a **3.4 kWh battery** with a real-world range of **100 km** .


That’s roughly nine full charges.


9 × 3.4 kWh = **30.6 kWh**


At ₹6 per unit:


30.6 × ₹6 = **₹183.60**


So the estimated monthly electricity cost is about **₹184** .


Real charging consumption will be somewhat higher because of charging losses. Allowing around **10–15%** gives a more realistic estimate of the electricity drawn from the grid.


The same calculation works for a car. You simply use the vehicle’s battery capacity and real-world range.


## **State-Wise EV Charging Tariffs**


EV charging tariffs vary from one state to another. Each State Electricity Regulatory Commission (SERC) sets the applicable rate, so your charging cost depends partly on where you charge. The Bureau of Energy Efficiency (BEE) maintains a consolidated list of state-wise EV tariffs.


[View the BEE state-wise EV tariff list](https://beeindia.gov.in/sites/default/files/annexure-A.pdf?utm_source=chatgpt.com)


**State** **EV Tariff (₹/kWh)** **Fixed Charge**


Delhi ₹4.50 (LT), ₹4.00 (HT) Nil


Gujarat ₹4.10 (LT), ₹4.00 (HT) ₹25/installation/month


Karnataka ₹5.00 ₹70–₹170/kW


Kerala ₹5.50 (LT), ₹6.00 (HT) ₹90/kW


Uttar Pradesh ₹5.50 Varies


Maharashtra ₹6.08 (LT), ₹6.90 (HT) ₹75/kW


Madhya Pradesh ₹6.79 (LT), ₹6.96 (HT) Nil


Haryana ₹6.62 (LT), ₹6.22 (HT) Nil


**LT** means Low Tension, while **HT** means High Tension. Rates and charges can change with updated tariff orders, so check the latest applicable rate when calculating your actual charging expense.


## **Does the Time of Charging Affect Your EV Charging Cost?**


In several states, yes.


Time-of-use (ToU) tariffs change electricity rates according to the time of day. The reference mentions Delhi, Maharashtra, Uttar Pradesh and Telangana among states offering ToU tariffs.


Off-peak hours are typically around 10 PM to 6 AM. During these hours, rates can be 20–30% lower than peak evening rates between 6 PM and 10 PM.


So if your DISCOM supports ToU metering, charging overnight can make a noticeable difference.


For example, scheduling a charge to start around 11 PM and finish in the morning can help you avoid the higher evening period. A smart charger with scheduling can handle this automatically.


## **Are There Free EV Charging Stations in India?**


Sometimes.


Charge Point Operators and EV manufacturers can offer free or discounted charging during promotional periods, launches, festive campaigns or as part of an ownership package.


Some government-supported charging locations can also have lower tariffs than privately operated stations.


These offers change.


Before starting a charging session, check the charging app for the current price and any active offer. Some ownership plans also include a fixed number of complimentary fast-charging sessions.


## **What Does EV Charging Cost Per Kilometre?**


Looking at **EV charging cost per kilometre** can be more useful than looking at the price of a single full charge.


The estimated running cost in the available figures is:


- **Home charging:** ₹0.50–₹1.50 per km


- **Public DC fast charging:** ₹1.50–₹3 per km


Your battery capacity, electricity rate and charging habits all affect the final figure.


For example, someone who charges almost entirely at home will have a very different running cost from someone who regularly uses highway fast chargers.


## **How Much Does an Electric Scooter Cost to Charge Each Month?**


For a rider travelling around **800–1,000 km every month** , the figures can vary significantly depending on where the charging happens.


A scooter with a **3.4 kWh battery** and around **100 km real-world range** would use roughly nine to ten full battery cycles over that distance.


For home charging, the estimated monthly cost is around **₹150–₹300** .


For riders who rely more heavily on public fast charging, the estimated monthly expense is around **₹400–₹800** .


The charging mix is the important part.


The more of your energy you get from public fast charging, the higher your monthly charging expense tends to be.


## **Simple Ways to Reduce EV Charging Costs**


You don’t need to change your entire routine.


A few habits can make a difference.


### **Charge at home when practical**


Home electricity is generally cheaper than public charging. Overnight charging can be even more useful when an off-peak tariff is available.


### **Watch your household electricity usage**


If EV charging pushes your household consumption into a higher tariff slab, the cost per unit can increase. A dedicated EV meter keeps the charging load separate from household consumption.


### **Use efficient ride modes**


Eco and Ride modes can reduce energy consumption per kilometre during everyday riding.


### **Make use of regenerative braking**


Regenerative braking sends some recovered energy back into the battery instead of losing all of it as heat during braking.


### **Check for a dedicated EV tariff**


Some states offer dedicated EV tariffs below standard domestic rates. If one is available in your area, compare it with your existing tariff.


## **Does Charging to 80% Save Money?**


For everyday trips where you don’t need a full battery, stopping at around 80% can make sense.


The last 20% of a lithium-ion battery generally charges more slowly because the battery management system reduces the charging input to protect the cells. The slower final stage also involves some efficiency losses.


You don’t need 100% every morning if your daily route only uses a fraction of the battery.


Charge according to the distance you actually need to cover.


## **The Real Cost Depends on How You Charge**


There is no single **EV charging cost in India** that applies to everyone.


Your bill changes with the vehicle, the electricity tariff, your monthly distance and where you plug in.


For everyday commuting, home charging generally keeps the running cost down. Public AC charging is useful when you need a charging point away from home. DC fast charging costs more per unit, but saves time when you’re travelling or need a quick top-up.


Once you know your vehicle’s battery capacity, real-world range and local electricity rate, the calculation becomes much easier.


You don’t need to guess what your EV will cost to run.


**Look at the units. Look at the tariff. Then look at how you actually drive.**


## **FAQs**


**What is the average cost of charging an electric vehicle in India?**


Home charging typically ranges from ₹4–₹10 per kWh. Public AC charging is around ₹8–₹15 per kWh, while DC fast charging is around ₹15–₹25 per kWh.


**Is home charging cheaper than public charging stations in India?**


Yes. Home electricity tariffs are generally lower than public charging rates. Public charging also includes operator service charges and GST.


**How much does DC fast charging cost in India?**


DC fast charging typically costs ₹15–₹25 per kWh. The rate varies according to the operator, location and charger speed.


**How much does it cost to fully charge an electric scooter at home?**


For a scooter with a 2–4 kWh battery, a full home charge can cost around ₹15–₹30 at a domestic electricity rate of ₹6–₹8 per unit.


**How much does it cost to install a home EV charger in India?**


Electric two-wheelers often don’t require a dedicated installation. A standard 5A socket can be sufficient. A wall-mounted charger or separate EV meter can involve additional costs depending on the wiring, charger and DISCOM requirements.
